title: Tenant-Isolated Mini Endpoint (TIME) PRD and Zero-Downtime Cutover Checklist
creator: Samira Patel
description: PRD for a lightweight, tenant-isolated hosted endpoint product (codename: TIME) that provides per-tenant micro endpoints for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank traffic. TIME aims to offer predictable unit economics, stronger data isolation guarantees, and a zero-downtime cutover path from shared hosted lanes to isolated mini endpoints. This ticket consolidates requirements, clarifications, and a launch readiness checklist for first pilot tenants.
goals: Deliver tenant-isolated mini endpoints that support the unified inference surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)
Ensure parity with hosted lane behavior for core API contracts while enabling tenant-specific tuning (cache size, batching hints, quantization profile)
Provide an automated zero-downtime cutover and rollback plan for moving traffic from shared lanes to TIME
Achieve p95 latency SLOs for short generation requests and maintain cost targets for POC tenants
in_scope: New endpoint provisioning workflow (API + Console) for tenant-isolated mini endpoints
Per-tenant configuration flags: KV cache size cap, preferred batching window, model variant pinning
Support for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank API calls with same contracts as hosted API
Telemetry: token-level cost attribution, per-tenant latency metrics, and error breakdowns
Canary rollout tooling with traffic split and health-based automatic rollback
out_of_scope: Enterprise on-prem appliance packaging (separate Private product effort)
Full multi-region active-active HA for initial pilot (region affinity only)
Cross-tenant federated caches or multi-tenant KV sharing
functional_requirements: TIME endpoints must accept the same REST/SDK payloads and response shapes as existing hosted endpoints
Provisioning API: POST /v1/tenants/:tid/endpoints returns endpoint_id and DNS/route information
Config API: allow read/write of tenant-specific config (cache_size, batch_window_ms, model_variant, quality_profile)
Fallback policy: endpoint must automatically fall back to a matched hosted lane variant if local capacity is exhausted, while emitting a fallback event to telemetry
Migration API: support phased cutover via traffic-splitting control for up to 5 canary slices and immediate rollback command
nonfunctional_requirements: Latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms for embeddings; p95 <= 450ms for short chat/generation (<= 32 tokens) in pilot region
Availability: 99.9% monthly for provisioned TIME endpoints
Cost target: 10-20% per-token unit cost improvement for caching-eligible workloads vs equivalent hosted lane at pilot scale
Observability: all requests must be tagged with tenant_id and endpoint_id and visible in Console within 60s
Security: tenant data must not be shared in logs; KMS-backed keys used for any ephemeral secrets
acceptance_criteria: API compatibility: existing SDK-based customers can switch to TIME endpoints without client code changes
Provisioning: create endpoint workflow completes within 90s and returns usable route

Cutover: execute a canary cutover for a pilot tenant moving 25% then 100% traffic with no more than 1% increased error rate compared to baseline and automatic rollback succeeds when health checks fail
Performance: pilot tenant meets the stated latency SLOs for at least 95% of requests during a 72-hour soak
Fallback correctness: when local capacity exhausted, requests seamlessly fallback to hosted lane variant with preserved response contract and telemetry shows fallback events
Billing & telemetry: per-token billing for TIME endpoints appears in the Console cost view and matches billing export within 1% for the test window
Security & compliance: KMS integration validated, and an access review completed by Security team
rollout_checklist: Console UI for endpoint provisioning and tiered config completed and UX-reviewed
E2E test plan executed: lifecycle tests (create, update, cutover, rollback, decommission)
Performance testing: perf harness run at target QPS with KV cache warmup and recorded baselines
Canary plan scheduled with two pilot tenants: one embeddings-heavy customer, one chat-heavy customer
Monitoring dashboards created: per-tenant latency, error budget burn, fallback events, token spend
Alerting: set SLO alerts and canary-specific playbook with runbook links
Security sign-off: secrets handling and KMS usage verified
Launch communication: customer success playbook and support runbook created
risks_mitigation: Risk: Unexpected latency increase due to smaller batching windows. Mitigation: allow dynamic batch_window_ms tuning per-tenant and observe with perf traces
Risk: Higher than expected cost from isolated allocations. Mitigation: recommend shared cache tiers and provide tenant cost threshold alerts; include autoscale down policy
Risk: Incomplete fallback behavior causing contract drift. Mitigation: build conformance tests that compare responses between TIME and hosted lane variants and block rollout on regressions
Risk: Operator complexity for many mini endpoints. Mitigation: add aggregation view in Console and a provisioning quota plus lifecycle garbage collection
